verdict.reasoning: Transcript: patient reports diarrhea for 'Three days ago now' but never states that it is worsening; she only says 'they're not getting any better.' No explicit worsening is mentioned.
Transcript: 'Three days ago now.' and 'It's very loose, but it started as being very watery.' This matches duration and change from watery to very loose.
Transcript: 'I lost count. Today alone, I've been at least four times.' This supports more than four episodes today and having lost count.

Transcript: 'Yes, I've been running at serious temperature. I'm literally boiling.' and 'Have you checked your temperature...?' 'No, because I've not got one.' Confirms feeling feverish and no measured temperature.

Transcript: 'Yes, I've been throwing up. I can't seem to be able to keep anything in me. Not even water...' and 'I was sick... maybe about two hours ago.' Confirms vomiting including fluids and last episode ~2 hours ago.
Transcript: 'I can't seem to be able to keep anything in me. Not even water... I've just been throwing up everything.' This supports inability to tolerate food or water.

Transcript: pain 'towards my navel area... I can't touch my navel area. It's just so sore' and 'When it comes, I feel the strong urge to go to the loo and then sort of releases me... It comes and goes.' Matches peri-umbilical, sore to touch, intermittent, urge to defecate.
Transcript: 'And any blood in the stool or in the urine that you've noticed?' Patient: 'No blood.' This includes denial of blood in stool.
Transcript: Same response 'No blood.' to question about blood 'in the stool or in the urine,' so she denies blood in urine.
Transcript: 'Any other symptoms at the moment, like rash?' Patient: 'No, no rash, no. Nothing.' Confirms no rash.
Transcript: 'My bowels is normally fine. I would normally go to the toilet every day.' and 'Episodes of diarrhea or constipation? Normally, no.' Indicates normal prior bowel habits.
Transcript: 'And when did you last pass urine, do you think?' Patient: 'At least an hour ago.' Confirms last urination ~1 hour ago.
Transcript: 'What sort of color is the urine?' Patient: 'To be honest, I can't know how to look, so I really couldn't see.' Confirms she does not know urine color.
Transcript: 'And have you got a normal diet?' Patient: 'Yeah, I eat well normally.' Supports diet normal prior to illness.

Transcript: 'Have you had to miss work because of this problem?' Patient: 'Well, yes, I've had to actually work from home today. I'm working from home today because I can't.' Confirms missed usual work and working from home.
Transcript: 'I get the odd, you know, menstrual cramps and all that, but... that comes and goes.' This supports a history of dysmenorrhea.

Transcript: 'Any surgery before or abdominal problems or any other medical issues?' Patient: 'Well, apart from the fact that this one is giving me abdominal pains. No previous abdominal pains before...' and bowels normally fine. No chronic GI history reported.

Transcript: Doctor asks about 'Any surgery before...' and patient does not report any; only current issue and menstrual cramps are mentioned. Absence of past surgical history in response supports that none is reported.
Transcript: 'Well, I take my vitamins, Vitamin D every day. That's about all that I regularly take.' Confirms daily vitamin D.

Transcript: 'Maybe I might take a naprine just to eat the pain.' (likely naproxen/naprosyn), but this is a different drug name; the transcript does not explicitly say 'naproxen.' Treating 'naprine' as naproxen is an inference beyond the exact wording.
Transcript: 'I've tried the ORs... The salt, sugar, ORs mix.' and 'I've taken that, like three times a day for the past two days.' Matches statement.
Transcript: 'And what's your job?' Patient: 'I'm a graphics designer.'
Transcript: 'And who do you live with at home?' Patient: 'I live with my brother and my mum.'
Transcript: 'Do you smoke or drink alcohol?' Patient: 'Well, I don't smoke, but, you know, I have a pint from time to time.' Supports occasional alcohol use.
Transcript: 'Do you smoke or drink alcohol?' Patient: 'Well, I don't smoke...' Confirms no tobacco use.
Transcript: 'And do you take any other drugs?' Patient: 'No, like I said, I only take vitamins...' Denies recreational/other drug use.

Transcript: 'my brother has actually been having similar symptoms for the past few days as well. And he does say, like, everyone in school's got it...' Confirms brother has similar GI symptoms and reports school outbreak.
Transcript: 'Any high temperatures or you feeling feverish?' Patient: 'Yes, I've been running at serious temperature. I'm literally boiling.' Indicates feverishness.
Transcript: 'Yes, I've been throwing up.' Confirms vomiting on review.
Transcript: abdominal pain around navel described in detail. This supports abdominal pain on review.
Transcript: 'And any blood in the stool or in the urine that you've noticed?' Patient: 'No blood.' Denies blood in stool.
Transcript: Same 'No blood.' response applies to urine as well, denying blood in urine.
Transcript: 'Any other medical problems? Have you had any other symptoms at the moment, like rash?' Patient: 'No, no rash, no. Nothing.' Confirms no rash.
Transcript: Doctor asks about temperature measurement; patient: 'No, because I've not got one.' No temperature is measured during this visit.
Transcript: 'And when did you last pass urine, do you think?' Patient: 'At least an hour ago.' Objective information that she passed urine about one hour ago.
Transcript: 'any blood in the stool or in the urine...?' Patient: 'No blood.' Objective documentation reflects no observed blood by patient report.
Transcript only documents history: 'No, no rash, no. Nothing.' There is no mention of a physical exam or that 'no rash was seen on exam'; that part is inferred, not stated.
Transcript: Doctor: 'it sounds like it might be an infectious gastroenteritis that you've got, which is usually caused by a virus...' This matches assessment of acute infectious gastroenteritis.

Transcript: 'we should also check that you're not getting dehydrated because if you're not keeping fluid down that you can get dehydrated.' and patient unable to keep fluids down. Shows concern for vomiting, poor intake, and dehydration risk.
Transcript: 'you need to carry on with your rehydration salts and just have very small amounts... just tiny, tiny sips, but just keep going with it.' Matches advice.

Transcript: 'And just have very simple food. If you're going to have anything like two toast or biscuit or something really light like that. Avoid fruit, vegetables, milk, anything like that...' Matches simple diet and avoidance instructions.
Transcript: 'we can make you an urgent appointment and then you can get the sample sent off...' Confirms urgent clinic appointment and stool sample.
Transcript: 'we should also check that you're not getting dehydrated' and 'we can check your hydration' at clinic. Indicates hydration status will be assessed.

Transcript: 'if in the meantime you're feeling more unwell, then we would get you seen urgently in ae.' and patient hopes not to go to A&E. This is advice to attend A&E if worsening/clinical deterioration; context is inability to keep fluids down.
Transcript: 'Okay, so you're happy to book an appointment through the support line?' Patient: 'Yes, please.' and 'We'll do that for you.' Indicates support in booking via a support line.
